answer.rationale: In the archive there are two memories directly about release management: b1 says rolling back cleared a checkout error spike, and b6 says staged gating caught bad builds. I want to verify those before committing, because the constraints here look like exactly the kind of situation they describe — a bad build pushed two hours ago with write-path latency climbing. The compliance rule says the security patch must not be reverted, but a full rollback isn't the only lever; staged gating / partial canary revocation (canary cohort pull-back per b6) can drop the bad build off the live population while preserving the security patch's release identity if it is in a separate component, and if not, a full rollback per b1 historically cleared the spike fast. Either way the prior evidence supports a release-direction intervention over failover or capacity. Failover (b2) is for regional degradation, not a same-region write-path regression; read-replica routing (b5) is for read load, not writes; circuit-breaker (b4) is for a partner dependency failure, not self-inflicted write latency; capacity (b3) is for a known retail peak, which isn't the shape of this incident. So the one intervention should be on the release. I will verify b1 and b6 to confirm the rollback/gating playbook details before executing.
